engine.symptomsMatch: Cold-start knock, metallic tapping, loss of oil pressure
engine.summary: Cold-start knock on a 306DT is the classic early warning. If oil pressure is already dropping, secondary damage is likely and replacement maths usually beats a bottom-end rebuild.

oil.commonOn: 4.4 SDV8 (448DT) in Range Rover / Range Rover Sport
oil.symptomsMatch: Oil in coolant, mayonnaise on the cap, rising oil level
oil.summary: The 4.4 SDV8 oil cooler is the main weak point. Catch it before coolant ingestion and a cooler job is enough; leave it and you are into a full engine replacement.

cooling.commonOn: TDV6, Ingenium diesel, and AJ126 petrol
cooling.symptomsMatch: Overheating, heater blowing cold, unexplained coolant loss
cooling.summary: JLR cooling faults range from a cheap thermostat housing to a head gasket. The value of the car decides whether you repair the cooling circuit or walk into a replacement quote.

timing.symptomsMatch: Rattle on cold start, check-engine light, rough idle
timing.summary: Pre-2019 Ingenium chain rattle is well documented and significantly improved from 2019. A chain kit at the right mileage is cheaper than waiting for a jumped chain and bent valves.

turbo.symptomsMatch: Whistle, boost loss, blue smoke, oily intercooler pipes
turbo.summary: Turbo failures are often oil-feed or carbon related. A quality turbo and feed-pipe refresh is usually worth doing; only high-mileage low-value cars fail the replacement maths.

electrical.commonOn: All JLR models, especially EAS and Terrain Response cars
electrical.symptomsMatch: Slow crank, warning lights, modules dropping offline
electrical.summary: Most electrical 'engine' complaints start with a tired battery or a poor earth. Diagnose the charging circuit before quoting an engine — this is usually a repair, not a replacement.

eas.commonOn: Range Rover L322/L405, Discovery 3/4, Range Rover Sport
eas.symptomsMatch: Car sitting low overnight, compressor running constantly, height faults
eas.summary: Air suspension is a known JLR cost centre. Compressors, valve blocks and leaks are repairable; only ignore it if the rest of the car is already past economic repair.

drivetrain.commonOn: Discovery 3/4 and Range Rover Sport with Terrain Response
drivetrain.symptomsMatch: Clunk on take-off, 4WD warning, binding on tight lock
drivetrain.summary: Transfer box actuator and viscous-coupling wear is common. A specialist rebuild is usually cheaper than a main-dealer box — run the value check before committing.

noise.symptomsMatch: Metallic knock from cold, tapping that fades when warm, oil-pressure warning
noise.summary: A cold-start knock on these diesels is not a harmless injector tick. Treat it as a bottom-end warning and get an oil-pressure test before you spend on cosmetics.

other.likelihood: Unknown — start with a specialist inspection
other.commonOn: All Land Rover and Range Rover models
other.symptomsMatch: Mixed or unclear symptoms, stored codes, intermittent faults
other.summary: If the fault does not match a known pattern, do not guess. A JLR specialist inspection with live data is cheaper than replacing the wrong part — then come back with the codes.
